Japan’s railway system relies heavily on organized boarding, platform markings, and passenger cooperation to keep trains moving efficiently. However, extreme crowding can still create discomfort and safety concerns, even when passengers remain orderly. 

​What looks like remarkable coordination is also a reminder of how much patience daily commuting can demand.

Callixte Nzamwita, a man from Rwanda, has lived in self-imposed isolation for 55 years after developing an intense fear of women at age 16. He built a fence around his small one-room home to maintain distance and told Afrimax TV that even being near women causes him distress. While his experience aligns with symptoms of gynophobia, no official medical diagnosis has been confirmed.

Despite his isolation, women in his community have quietly supported him for years by leaving food and essentials inside his fenced property. Their help has allowed him to live independently while respecting the boundaries he set. The story has drawn international attention as a rare case of extreme phobia and social withdrawal.

This viral video shows security officers in Colombia removing a "narcowig" (or narcopeluca) from a passenger attempting to smuggle illicit drugs.

The incident took place at the Rafael Núñez International Airport in Cartagena, Colombia. Security agents became suspicious of the passenger's unusual hairstyle and subsequently used an X-ray scanner, which revealed hidden packages underneath a hairpiece glued to his scalp.

Upon cutting open the toupee, officers discovered 19 capsules containing cocaine, weighing over 200 grams in total and valued at roughly $10,000. 

The passenger was arrested on the spot for trafficking controlled substances.

On November 9, 2017, nine-year-old Dezde-zyer Mays was crossing Babbitt Road in Euclid, Ohio, on her way to the bus stop when a car hit her and drove away.

 The impact broke her neck, both legs and every bone in her face, knocked out her teeth and split her chin. She died in the hospital on November 21. 

​The driver, Lacynthia Tidmore, went to a gas station. Court records say she saw the damage to her car, then called her mother to take her to work. She did not return to help Mays or call 911; witnesses called for help. 

​At her sentencing on May 24, 2018, Mays's mother and great-aunt spoke about the little girl they lost and the pain her death left behind. Tidmore received an eight-year prison sentence. Ohio records now show her under state supervision, with October 5, 2026, listed as her expected release date. 

​Eight years cannot give a child her life back or undo what her family has endured. Does this sentence feel like justice?

mushisamagic.caption:
The Jessica Lunsford case remains one of the most heartbreaking true crime cases in America. In February 2005, 9 year old Jessica disappeared from her bedroom in Homosassa, Florida. Weeks later, investigators found her buried in a shallow grave behind a mobile home where John Evander Couey had been staying. She was found clutching the purple stuffed dolphin she had taken from her bedroom that night. 

 
​What makes this case even more disturbing is what Couey later told investigators. In a recorded confession, he said Jessica was still alive when he buried her and that he let her keep her stuffed dolphin because she wanted to take it with her. Her cause of death was determined to be asphyxiation. The confession itself was later ruled inadmissible at trial because of a violation of his right to counsel, but other evidence was allowed to be presented. 

​John Evander Couey was ultimately convicted in 2007 of first degree murder, kidnapping, sexual battery on a child, and burglary. The Jessica Lunsford murder case shocked the country and helped push for stronger laws aimed at protecting children and monitoring convicted sex offenders. It is a case that still gets discussed today because behind all the courtroom footage and headlines was a 9 year old girl whose life was taken far too soon.
